findings: getMemberId() undefined — member-schedule.js calls getMemberId() but the function is not defined in that file or imported from another module. Likely defined in api.js or auth.js, but without explicit import or global declaration, this will throw ReferenceError at runtime.

TimeSpan string format mismatch — frontend sends time as "HH:MM" string from <input type="time">, but backend expects TimeSpan. ASP.NET Core model binding likely handles this, but without explicit test, there's risk of TimeSpan.Zero if parsing fails. Verify with integration test or add explicit logging.

No member ownership validation — MemberSchedulePreferenceController endpoints (Create, Update, Delete, GetByMember) don't verify that the requesting member's JWT claim matches the target MemberId. A member could create, update, delete, or view another member's preferences by manipulating request parameters. Extract memberId from User.FindFirst("memberId") and validate against request/entity.
